audits.title: [Audit of artificial nutrition in an intensive care unit].
audits.standard: ICU artificial nutrition protocol (corrected Harris-Benedict and fixed 25 kcal/kg prescription)
audits.setting: Intensive Care Unit, Hospital Clínico San Carlos, Madrid

cycle1.result: Energy and nitrogen provision below theoretical levels.

audits.intervention: Unit agreed to increase nitrogen provision in the protocol.

cycle2.result: Greater agreement between theoretical and actual provision; deviation in energy and nitrogen significantly less; hyperproteic diets rose from 9-13 g to 18-20 g nitrogen.

audits.other_findings: Over-nutrition occurred in both series when enteral and parenteral nutrition were combined.
audits.citation: Blesa Malpica AL, Salaverría Garzón I, Prado López LM, Simón García MJ, Reta Pérez O, Ramos Polo J. [Audit of artificial nutrition in an intensive care unit]. Nutr Hosp. 2001;16(2):46-54. PMID: 11443833.

audits.title: Failure of a quality improvement process to increase nutrition delivery to intensive care patients.
audits.standard: Predicted daily energy requirement for patients staying over 3 days
audits.setting: Intensive Care Service, Royal Prince Alfred Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Nutrition started 2.2 +/- 1.3 days after admission; 100% of requirement reached by 4.8 +/- 3.3 days; nutrition on 82.3% of patient-days; daily average 71.7% of energy requirement; interrupted on 30% of patient-days.

audits.intervention: Clinical Practice Improvement model used to analyse reasons for inadequate feeding and change practice, targeting interruptions for extubation and upper GI intolerance.

cycle2.result: Interruptions for these reasons significantly reduced but no significant overall improvement in time to nutritional goals or energy received.

audits.other_findings: 379 consecutive patients over 12 months in total.
audits.citation: Ferrie S, McWilliam D. Failure of a quality improvement process to increase nutrition delivery to intensive care patients. Anaesth Intensive Care. 2006;34(2):191-196. doi:10.1177/0310057x0603400211. PMID: 16617639.

audits.title: The value of audit and feedback reports in improving nutrition therapy in the intensive care unit: a multicenter observational study.

cycle1.result: EN adequacy 45.1% (calories) and 44.8% (protein); EN without PN 71.9%; EN started within 48 h 60.3%.

audits.intervention: Individualised benchmarked performance reports e-mailed to each ICU.

cycle2.result: EN adequacy 51.9% (calories) and 51.5% (protein); EN without PN 81.3%; EN within 48 h 66.8%.

audits.other_findings: No significant change in motility agents or small bowel feeding for high gastric residual volumes.
audits.citation: Sinuff T, Cahill NE, Dhaliwal R, Wang M, Day AG, Heyland DK. The value of audit and feedback reports in improving nutrition therapy in the intensive care unit: a multicenter observational study. JPEN J Parenter Enteral Nutr. 2010;34(6):660-668. doi:10.1177/0148607110373484. PMID: 21097766.

audits.title: [Impact of quality improvement process upon the state of nutritional support in a critical care unit].
audits.standard: Local nutritional support protocol (fulfilment of prescribed nutritional support, ≥80% of prescribed energy)
audits.setting: Critical care unit, Hospital Interzonal General de Agudos Dr. Rodolfo Rossi, La Plata

cycle1.result: Phase 1 (previous audit): overall mortality 40.0%; mean energy intake 574.7 ± 395.3 kcal/24 h.

audits.intervention: Presentation and publication of audit results, a new nutritional support protocol, and continuous education (expert talks, courses, protocol training)

cycle2.result: Higher fulfilment of prescribed nutritional support, more patients receiving ≥80% of prescribed energy and fewer lost days; mortality 20.5% (p = 0.054); mean energy intake 591.1 ± 315.3 kcal/24 h (p > 0.05).

audits.other_findings: Haemodynamic instability remained the main obstacle to starting and completing nutritional support.
audits.citation: Martinuzzi A, Martinuzzi A, Ferraresi E, Orsati M, Palaoro A, Chaparro J, et al.. [Impact of quality improvement process upon the state of nutritional support in a critical care unit]. Nutr Hosp. 2012;27(4):1219-1227. doi:10.3305/nh.2012.27.4.5817. PMID: 23165565.

audits.title: Nutrition During Critical Care: An Audit on Actual Energy and Protein Intakes.
audits.standard: Weight-based energy and protein targets; receiving at least 80% of targets
audits.setting: Mixed ICU, University Hospital of Liège

cycle1.result: Fed patients received 14.3 kcal/kg/day and 0.53 g/kg/day protein; orally fed patients 9.7 kcal/kg/day and 0.35 g/kg/day; of orally fed patients staying 7 days or more, 51% and 94% never received 80% of energy and protein targets.

audits.other_findings: Protein deficit was larger than energy deficit.
audits.citation: Rougier L, Preiser JC, Fadeur M, Verbrugge AM, Paquot N, Ledoux D, et al.. Nutrition During Critical Care: An Audit on Actual Energy and Protein Intakes. JPEN J Parenter Enteral Nutr. 2021;45(5):951-960. doi:10.1002/jpen.1962. PMID: 32776591.
